Private installed fixture checkpoint; source preparation only.

R3 regression triggers, stated before adding driver tests: a manual summarize
request with auto enabled can resume ordinary work; an old summary or a summary
from another root can hide a false completion; V2 execution success without an
ordinary assistant step can be mistaken for completion. A fork's source lineage
can be mistaken for child ancestry; unrelated tool results or an unadvertised
agent can manufacture apparent child proof. Pure route/projection/provider-input
tests will challenge those boundaries with independently transcribed contracts.
No new test will run a provider, host, installer or notification runtime.

Red triggers for the inert tests: duplicate manifest keys could silently
retarget an input; unfilled template could qualify an arbitrary binary; changed
archive/image bytes could run after review; escaped input could read outside the
checkout; native interruption/compaction or mismatched execution could count as
terminal attention; an exited but unawaited fixture child could leak ownership.
Tests exercise parser/native-envelope and inert child boundaries. They do not
mock a qualified profile, production clock, native frame grant or external effect.

with exact candidate builds; official archive SHA/SRI/executable identities are

`reviewed-host-custody.json` preserves the input/review/primary-metadata hashes and

still has null source metadata. Root must bind that verified source identity in

`embedded` and independently `rebuilt` bytes must agree before host launch. Supply
the actual packed SDK tar and its SHA512 SRI, source manifest hash and exact npm
lock bytes. A file tar uses actual `resolved:file:` metadata and may lack integrity;

The runner also compares host inputs to the reviewed byte-only pin ledger.
The manifest is custody input; it cannot grant product runtime eligibility.
Darwin `nativeApp` is `{root,executable:{path,sha256},sidecar:{path,sha256}}`.
Actual installer still checks its seal/signature; fixture hashing is insufficient.

Installed native qualification requires manual dispatch with reviewed parent evidence;
ordinary final-head PR CI does not prove installed E2E. Keep checkpoint 4d4 parent
VCS identity distinct from final CI: the reviewed 4d4->577 equivalence covers only

The parent archive/pins are not produced by this worker; absent/wrong evidence

No fixture defaults to user config, auth, bus, provider or existing runtime root.

First concrete gate failure stops later phases with nonzero/unqualified; neither
missing archives nor denied qualification is skip/pass. The baseline product has
no origin token in the embedded bundle, nil profile qualification and empty clock
cells. Current public `config inspect` resolves shared `config.json`, whereas the
managed consumer reads `<control-root>/agent-notifications.json`. It has no path
flag. Runner refuses that mismatch, does not set AGENT_NOTIFICATIONS_CONFIG and
never writes an unlocked policy. The narrow product integration needed is an
existing public config/store path selecting the managed policy with CAS and
compatible generation/lock semantics, retaining setup route fields.

The native capture is an independent read-only observer, not the product observer.
Its real same-parent profile query is bounded and waits for actual close, with no
eligible fields supplied. A production clock snapshot is E0 evidence only; no
public pre-model command currently proves selected complete T/source conversion.
The explicit stop in `qualify` preserves this unresolved gate. Root must resolve
it through authoritative product integration/evidence, never delete it merely to
reach scenarios. The business/lifecycle body below it is staged and unexecuted.

Continuation red triggers: transcribing x64 to an unsupported fixture arch could
drop an ARM or Windows cell; mixing registry/archive and executable hashes could
launch different bytes; treating a copied fork message as fresh could revive old
completion. Parser fixtures compare supplied custody facts and reject excluded
canonical message identities; these tests make no native/runtime grant.

Final-assistant red trigger: a permanent provider400 plus a failed native step
could be counted while its ordinary assistant projection is missing, incomplete,
from another session/message, a compaction summary or a user interruption. The
staged driver must also read the existing public history/message route and match
the native final message identity and original numeric completion time. Independent
parser examples reject those mismatches without invoking any native host or grant.

Review R1 red triggers: a clean source copy lacks hosted TASK-INPUTS; a manifest
tracked with its own exact commit creates an impossible source/artifact cycle;
same native IDs can conceal changed V1 parent/completion metadata. Inert tests
use real private external tar/file IO, separate source/metadata parser examples
and independently supplied V1 envelopes/projections. They prove no real Go build,
clean Git checkout, SDK/native/profile/clock grant or installed effect. V1 compares
original parentID/completed against the independently fetched projection. R4 corrects V2 to its actual durable session-log positions and typed assistant
projection; it invents no data.executionID or V1 role/sessionID/parent fields.

R4 binds the two public drivers below the unchanged unconditional production clock
pre-model stop. V1 floor/current primary files have identical compaction, prompt,
task and route bytes. V1 uses POST `/session/:id/summarize` with providerID/modelID
and `auto:false`, joins the new `summary:true` assistant to its real compaction
control user part, and compares original parent/completion metadata against a
fresh history read. V2 stages POST `/api/session/:id/compact` with `{}`; the native
host chooses its admitted input ID. No fabricated neutral frame, custom compaction
hook or provider-supplied native timestamp participates. The provider distinguishes
V1's single-user conversation/anchored-summary request from V2's supplied new-summary
prompt. Responses follow each generation's actual inline template: V1 uses
Important Details; V2 uses Requirements/Decisions/Important Context.
Two ordinary native user turns surround the summary phase; each must have one
desktop submission and one webhook, while the summary phase must have zero.
Reports label a later observed 1/0/1 as finite observations with product final
checkpoint/owned close still unproved. This worker observed none of those effects.

Foreground child requests use only the actually advertised V1 `task` schema
(`description,prompt,subagent_type`) or V2 `subagent` schema
(`agent,description,prompt`). Optional background, continuation, command and model
override fields are omitted. V1 config defines `an-e2e-child` as a subagent and
permits only that task target under the existing default deny policy. V2 uses
plural `agents`, ordered `permissions`, an explicit subagent allow for the exact
TEST child on the parent agent and a child override denying every tool. The child
inherits the private provider model. The provider answers the child's genuine
prompt without tools, then holds its parent's next request after the REAL host
returns the completed tool result. The source renderers bind its tool_call_id and
child ID; native completed task metadata (V1) or executed input/called/Tool.Success
identity (V2) must independently join that exact call, parent and child. Native
creation and public session projection must agree on
the actual parentID, location and configured agent. A root fork cannot satisfy
this join. Release allows one ordinary parent completion, followed by a fresh
root turn; child zero counts are sampled before parent release. This is provider
IO control, not a product settlement checkpoint. V2 /prompt acknowledges durable inbox admission before agent execution; its
returned HTTP thread does not end the foreground-child wait. V1 retains its
blocking-message exit check. Provider/transport/admission faults still stop before
child projection or parent release. The hold retains the existing
12s bound; each driver phase has one original 40s observation deadline, with no
reset after route response or child result. Cleanup releases the provider barrier
and awaits owned prompt/server handles; uncertainty never causes a prompt retry.
